tldr: Friday 20 Nov was a distinct, sharper shock than Thu-19 Nov's Fed/Philly-Fed selloff: Reuters' Nvidia SEC-accounting-probe report (-14%, ~$500bn erased) and Google's reported 20% Broadcom TPU-order cut (AVGO -11.4%, MRVL -10%) landed on a negative-gamma options-expiry day, driving VIX +26.2% to 35.89 (highest since March).

Biggest risk to the book: the owner's 2.487x-levered silver position is FAILING its survivability metric right as gold/silver/miners fell in lockstep with equities (GLD -3.67%, SLV -6.74%, GDX -5.00%) on what analysts read as margin-call-driven forced liquidation, not a fresh metals catalyst.

HK tech (0700/0981/1810.HK) and SGX (STI -2.07%, DBS/OCBC/UOB all down) both took direct, idiosyncratic hits this week -- Tencent's own 225% capex surge and chip-curb commentary, and a new US AI-chip export rule naming Singapore data centres -- on top of generic global risk-off.

Counterintuitive cross-current: despite the brutal price action, BofA/EPFR and Lipper's week-ended-18-Nov fund flows (finally covering the whole selloff week) show net equity INFLOWS (+$66.6bn/+$59.2bn) -- flows have not capitulated the way sentiment has (Fear & Greed fell to 14, Extreme Fear).

Rare earths (MP -7.39%) gave back a 3-day, trade-talk-driven rally to Friday's broad-market beta, not a reversal of the underlying thesis -- a 3-insider cluster buy ($3.35M, Nov 10) and a Bridgewater 13F add (+9.9%) both predate the bounce.

A cross-member Congress NVDA-sell cluster (Rulli, Khanna's spouse, Meuser's spouse) in the weeks before both Jensen Huang's resignation and Friday's SEC-probe report is worth watching, without implying advance knowledge.
